resolutions.why_not_branch_a: Acceptance (a)'s own cheaper route was evaluated concretely and FALSIFIED, not declined on preference. It offered 'a check that the `low_item_coverage` message's percentage equals `meta.coverage`'. `low_item_coverage` fires on exactly one committed document, `xref-index-collapse`, and that document carries ZERO incorporated_by_reference spans — so the mutant (which differs only by excluding IBR spans) computes an identical figure there. Measured under the mutant: meta.coverage 0.0303 and the message 'only 3.0% of the document lies inside an item span (1,003 of 33,061 chars)' — byte-identical to the unmutated run. Such a check would stay GREEN under the very mutant it exists to catch, so it does not satisfy its own acceptance. Every fixture that DOES diverge is one where the warning never fires, so no output carries the thresholded number to assert against. The only (a) that binds is the second one acceptance names — making validate() read the published figure — which is a signature change to the layer-8 entry point with ~10 _demo call sites behind it: a pipeline change requiring a re-measured, re-cited blast radius, which the round-2 brief pre-ruled as more than the finding warrants.
